# Bessel Functions

![Bessel Functions function icon](../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/bessel/00_Bessel%20function.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../index.md) · [All functions](../../index.md)

Twelve fixed scalar functions: cylindrical J/Y/H, modified I/K, spherical j/y/h, Airy Ai and Bi, ordinary Struve H, Kelvin be/ke. FROG profiles frog_bessel_v1 / ni_documented_abs_v1 evaluate r=\|x\|; this documentary NI adapter policy is not a mathematical evenness identity or measured NI parity. x is required; unwired order and type default to 0 (FROG choices). No degrees/radians conversion. Scalar NI baseline; FROG also applies scalar order/kind to real numeric x arrays/clusters, preserving dimensions, typed empties and fields. Real leaves promote to f64; result leaves are f64 or complex&lt;f64&gt;. Integer ports remain exact i32; no new broadcasting or complex arguments. Nonfinite input and singularities return NaN; overflow gives signed Infinity, underflow warns and subnormals are preserved. No error terminals. FROG diagnostic categories: SINGULAR, NONFINITE_INPUT, INVALID_KIND, OVERFLOW, UNDERFLOW, NUMERICAL_FAILURE; these are not NI codes.

Douze fonctions scalaires fixes : J/Y/H cylindriques, I/K modifiées, j/y/h sphériques, Airy Ai et Bi, Struve H ordinaire, Kelvin be/ke. Les profils FROG frog_bessel_v1 / ni_documented_abs_v1 évaluent r=\|x\| ; cette adaptation de la documentation NI n’est ni une identité de parité mathématique ni une compatibilité NI mesurée. x est requis ; ordre et type non câblés valent 0 (choix FROG). Aucune conversion degrés/radians. Socle NI scalaire ; l’extension FROG applique ordre et espèce scalaires aux tableaux/clusters x réels numériques en préservant dimensions, vides typés et champs. Les feuilles réelles sont promues en f64 ; résultats à feuilles f64 ou complex&lt;f64&gt;. Ports entiers strictement i32 ; sans nouveau broadcasting ni argument complexe. Entrées non finies et singularités donnent NaN ; dépassement : infini signé ; sous-dépassement : avertissement ; sous-normaux conservés. Aucun terminal d’erreur. Catégories FROG : SINGULAR, NONFINITE_INPUT, INVALID_KIND, OVERFLOW, UNDERFLOW, NUMERICAL_FAILURE ; pas des codes NI.

## Browse this palette

This entry opens a palette folder; it is not an executable dataflow function.

| Entry | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Bessel J](../../math/special/bessel_cyl_j.md) | Cylindrical Bessel function of the first kind, real order v (fractional and signed orders accepted). At r=0: 1 for v=0; 0 for positive v or negative integers; singular for negative noninteger v. Formula: J_v(r). Example: J_0(1)=0.7651976865579666. |
| [Bessel Y](../../math/special/bessel_cyl_y.md) | Cylindrical Bessel function of the second kind (Neumann), real order v. Requires r&gt;0; r=0 is singular. Negative and fractional orders are accepted. Formula: Y_v(r). Example: Y_0(1)=0.08825696421567696. |
| [Bessel H](../../math/special/hankel_cyl.md) | Cylindrical Hankel function. type=0 selects the first kind J+iY; type=1 selects the second kind J-iY. One complex F64 output preserves both components. Requires r&gt;0 and type in {0,1}; r=0 is singular. This evaluates a function, not a Hankel transform. Formula: J_v(r)+i*Y_v(r) for type=0; J_v(r)-i*Y_v(r) for type=1. Example: H_0^(1)(1)=0.7651976865579666+0.08825696421567696i. |
| [Bessel I](../../math/special/bessel_mod_i.md) | Modified Bessel function of the first kind, real order v. Public results are unscaled. At r=0: 1 for v=0; 0 for positive v or negative integers; singular for negative noninteger v. Negative noninteger orders do not use absolute order. Formula: I_v(r). Example: I_0(1)=1.2660658777520084. |
| [Bessel K](../../math/special/bessel_mod_k.md) | Modified Bessel function of the second kind, signed integer order n. K_-n=K_n. The supplied Kv(x) glyph is preserved; its connector remains integer. Requires r&gt;0; r=0 is singular. Public results are unscaled; representable subnormals are retained. Formula: K_n(r). Example: K_0(1)=0.4210244382407083. |
| [Bessel j](../../math/special/bessel_sph_j.md) | Spherical Bessel function of the first kind, signed integer order n; j_0(r)=sin(r)/r. Distinct from cylindrical J. At r=0: 1 for n=0; 0 for n&gt;0; singular for n&lt;0. Negative orders use spherical reflection relations. Formula: sqrt(pi/(2*r))*J_(n+1/2)(r). Example: j_0(1)=0.8414709848078965. |
| [Bessel y](../../math/special/bessel_sph_y.md) | Spherical Bessel function of the second kind, signed integer order n; y_0(r)=-cos(r)/r. Distinct from cylindrical Y. At r=0: singular for n&gt;=0; 1 for n=-1; 0 for n&lt;=-2, using negative-order reflection. Formula: sqrt(pi/(2*r))*Y_(n+1/2)(r). Example: y_0(1)=-0.5403023058681398. |
| [Bessel h](../../math/special/hankel_sph.md) | Spherical Hankel function, signed integer order n. type=0 gives j+iy; type=1 gives j-iy. One complex F64 output preserves both components. Requires r&gt;0 and type in {0,1}; r=0 is singular for every integer order. Distinct from cylindrical H. Formula: j_n(r)+i*y_n(r) for type=0; j_n(r)-i*y_n(r) for type=1. Example: h_0^(1)(1)=0.8414709848078965-0.5403023058681398i. |
| [Airy Ai, Bi](../../math/special/airy_ai_bi.md) | Returns both Airy functions on independent real F64 outputs ai and bi. Ai decreases and Bi increases for positive arguments; an overflow of Bi does not invalidate a calculable Ai. At r=0: Ai=0.3550280538878172, Bi=0.6149266274460007. No order input or derivative outputs. Standard Airy functions are not even; this adapter deliberately uses \|x\|. Formula: Ai(r), Bi(r). Example: Ai(1)=0.1352924163128814; Bi(1)=1.2074235949528713. |
| [Struve](../../math/special/struve_h.md) | Ordinary Struve H function, real order v. This is distinct from Hankel H and modified Struve L; there is no kind selector. At r=0: 0 for v&gt;-1; 2/pi for v=-1; 0 for v=-3/2-m (integer m&gt;=0); singular for other v&lt;-1. Formula: H_v(r) (ordinary Struve). Example: Struve H_0(1)=0.5686566270482879. |
| [Kelvin be](../../math/special/kelvin_be.md) | Kelvin be at signed integer order n. The real component is ber and the imaginary component is bei; one complex F64 output, with real input x. At r=0: 1+0i for n=0; 0+0i otherwise. Negative orders use be_-n=(-1)^n*be_n. Formula: ber_n(r)+i*bei_n(r)=J_n(r*exp(3*pi*i/4)). Example: be_0(1)=0.9843817812130868+0.2495660400366597i. |
| [Kelvin ke](../../math/special/kelvin_ke.md) | Kelvin ke at signed integer order n. The real component is ker and the imaginary component is kei; one complex F64 output, with real input x. The order-dependent phase is retained. Requires r&gt;0; r=0 is singular. Negative orders use ke_-n=(-1)^n*ke_n. This is neither reciprocal be nor real-axis K. Formula: ker_n(r)+i*kei_n(r)=exp(-n*pi*i/2)*K_n(r*exp(pi*i/4)). Example: ke_0(1)=0.2867062087283160-0.4949946365187199i. |
